## agent-ml-research
ML research experiment management tools

attachment.content:
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

{"success": true, "data": {"stdout": "\section{Experimental Setup}

\subsection{Models and Datasets}

We use \textbf{Pythia-410M-deduped} (405M parameters, $D{=}1024$) as the primary model and \textbf{Pythia-1B-deduped} (1042M parameters, $D{=}2048$) for scale-transfer validation.
Both are decoder-only transformers pretrained on the deduplicated Pile.

From the Pile (uncopyrighted split, \texttt{monology/pile-uncopyrighted}), we sample three disjoint subsets:
\begin{itemize}[nosep]
  \item \textbf{Training pool}: 50{,}000 sequences of 512 tokens for fine-tuning.
  \item \textbf{Evaluation set}: 5{,}000 held-out sequences for perplexity measurement.
  \item \textbf{Spectral probe set}: 1{,}000 held-out sequences for effective rank computation.
\end{itemize}
All sequences are tokenized with the GPTNeoX tokenizer (vocabulary size 50{,}304) and truncated or padded to 512 tokens.
We retain only sequences with at least 256 non-padding tokens ($\geq$50\% fill ratio) to ensure sufficient context for representation extraction.

\subsection{Recursive Training Protocol}

Generation~0 is the pretrained checkpoint with no additional fine-tuning.
For each subsequent generation $t = 1, \ldots, T$ with $T{=}10$:
\begin{enumerate}[nosep]
  \item \textbf{Synthetic generation.} Sample 50{,}000 sequences from $M_{t-1}$ via ancestral sampling (temperature $= 1.0$, top-$k = 50$, no nucleus filtering, max length 512 tokens, batch size 32).
  \item \textbf{Data mixing.} Combine synthetic samples with real data at condition-specific ratio $r_t$ (see \S\ref{sec:conditions}).  The number of real samples mixed in is $\lfloor n_{\text{syn}} \cdot r_t / (1 - r_t) \rfloor$, drawn uniformly without replacement from the training pool.
  \item \textbf{Fine-tuning.} Train $M_{t-1}$ for 1 epoch on the mixed corpus $\rightarrow M_t$.
  \item \textbf{Checkpoint and evaluate.} Save $M_t$; measure all metrics on held-out data.
\end{enumerate}

Training hyperparameters are fixed across all conditions: AdamW optimizer with learning rate $5{\times}10^{-5}$, weight decay $0.01$, batch size~8 with gradient accumulation~4 (effective batch size~32), linear warmup over 5\% of steps followed by linear decay, and gradient clipping at $\|\mathbf{g}\|_{\max} = 1.0$.
The number of optimizer steps per generation varies with the mixing ratio: ${\sim}1{,}562$ steps for pure synthetic ($r_t = 0$) to ${\sim}3{,}125$ steps at $r_t = 0.50$.

\subsection{Evaluation Metrics}

\paragraph{Effective Rank (RankMe).}
Following \citet{rankme2023}, we forward-pass the 1{,}000 spectral probe samples through $M_t$, extract last-layer hidden states, mean-pool across sequence length to obtain $\mathbf{Z} \in \mathbb{R}^{1000 \times D}$, compute its SVD, and report
\begin{equation}
  \rho(\mathbf{Z}) = \exp\!\Bigl(-\sum_i p_i \log p_i\Bigr), \quad p_i = \frac{\sigma_i}{\sum_j \sigma_j},
\end{equation}
where $\sigma_i$ are the singular values of $\mathbf{Z}$.
Lower effective rank signals representation collapse.
We measure spectral decline relative to Generation~1 (post-adaptation baseline) rather than Generation~0 (pretrained), as the pretrained-to-fine-tuned transition induces a shift in representation anisotropy unrelated to recursive collapse.
We use RankMe rather than SIGMA's Track~I bound~\cite{sigma2026} because (a)~no public implementation of SIGMA exists as of May 2026, (b)~RankMe is architecture-agnostic and hyperparameter-free, and (c)~RankMe's spectral entropy formulation provides a smooth, monotonic collapse indicator suitable for closed-loop control.

\paragraph{Log-Determinant Proxy.}
From the same SVD decomposition, we compute
\begin{equation}
  \mathcal{D}(\mathbf{Z}) = \sum_{i:\,\sigma_i > \epsilon} \log \sigma_i, \quad \epsilon = 10^{-10},
\end{equation}
which equals $\tfrac{1}{2}\log\det(\mathbf{Z}^\top\mathbf{Z})$ up to the threshold $\epsilon$.

\subsection{Statistical Design}

Each condition is run with 3 random seeds (42, 123, 7), paired across conditions (i.e., all four conditions share the same seed set) to reduce variance from initialization and data ordering.
We report mean $\pm$ standard deviation across seeds.

Significance testing uses paired $t$-tests on per-seed final metrics.
We adopt $\alpha=0.10$ following our pre-registered protocol, given the pragmatic minimum of 3 seeds.
Effect sizes are reported as Cohen's $d$ with 95\% bootstrap confidence intervals (10{,}000 resamples).

\paragraph{Phase~0 go/no-go criteria.}
Before launching Phase~1, we execute a single-seed ($s{=}42$) pure-synthetic run ($r_t = 0\;\forall\, t$, 10 generations) and require all of the following:
\begin{enumerate}[nosep]
  \item Monotonically decreasing effective rank across Generations~1--10.
  \item Acceleration ratio $\geq 1.5{\times}$: mean per-generation rank decline in Generations~6--10 divided by that in Generations~1--5.
  \item Held-out perplexity increase $> 20\%$ from Generation~1 to Generation~10.
\end{enumerate}
Failure on any criterion aborts the experiment and triggers hyperparameter revision.
Controller parameters $k$ and $\tau$ are calibrated from the Phase~0 spectral trajectory.

\paragraph{Pre-registered hypotheses.}
We pre-register two primary comparisons at Generation~$T{=}10$:
\begin{enumerate}[nosep]
  \item Adaptive vs.\ fixed uniform: $\geq$3 perplexity point improvement.
  \item Closed-loop (adaptive) vs.\ open-loop (linear-increasing): $\geq$1.5 perplexity point improvement.
\end{enumerate}

\paragraph{Compute budget.}
The full experiment comprises 1 Phase~0 pilot chain (single seed, 10 generations) and 12 Phase~1 chains (4 conditions $\times$ 3 seeds $\times$ 10 generations), totaling 130 generation-steps.
Each generation-step involves sampling 50{,}000 synthetic sequences, fine-tuning for 1 epoch (${\sim}$1{,}562--3{,}125 optimizer steps depending on the mixing ratio), and evaluating all metrics including 1{,}000-sample generation for Distinct-4.
